subject: principles-of-flight

concepts.concept: Rudder input produces yaw first; the resulting aerodynamic imbalance then develops roll and, if left uncorrected, can progress into a spiral dive.

source.document: POF mock exams written by Rihan.pdf
source.notes: The source explicitly states the primary and further effects of rudder: yaw, then roll, followed by spiral dive.

brief.student_must_understand: The sequence is causal and ordered: rudder -> yaw -> roll -> possible spiral dive if the imbalance is not corrected.
preserve: Aircraft attitude readable from above/three-quarter view
refine: Use three clean frames with arrows between stages
Show rudder deflection only at the initiating stage
Avoid implying that a brief rudder input automatically guarantees a spiral dive

concepts.mapping_reason: Both target rows test the exact same ordered rudder-effect sequence.

concepts.concept: Aileron input produces roll first; secondary yaw then develops and, if the resulting imbalance is left uncorrected, the aircraft can progress into a spiral dive.

source.document: POF mock exams written by Rihan.pdf
source.notes: The source explicitly gives roll, then yaw, followed by spiral dive for aileron-only input.

brief.student_must_understand: The sequence is ordered: aileron -> roll -> yaw -> possible spiral dive if uncorrected.
preserve: Final spiral state shown as a consequence, not an instantaneous effect
refine: Do not merge this with adverse-yaw-at-high-AoA teaching

concepts.mapping_reason: Questions 1120 and 1149 ask the same aileron-only primary/further-effect relationship.

concepts.concept: Moving the control column forward and left simultaneously lowers the elevator, raises the left aileron, and lowers the right aileron.

source.location: Question 114; cross-checked with ac_61-23c_phak_canada.pdf Figures 1-25 and 1-30
source.notes: Question source states the exact surface movements. PHAK Figure 1-30 confirms left-stick aileron motion; Figure 1-25 confirms forward-column elevator-down motion.

brief.student_must_understand: Forward-left column displacement combines two independent control responses: pitch-forward elevator-down plus left-roll aileron differential.
refine: Show one input arrow at the column and three synchronized surface callouts
Use rear/three-quarter aircraft view so all surfaces are readable
Make left/right aircraft sides impossible to confuse

concepts.mapping_reason: Question 2028 uniquely tests the combined forward-left control-column geometry.

concepts.concept: Aspect ratio compares wingspan with mean aerodynamic chord; for comparable lift conditions, a higher-aspect-ratio wing produces less induced drag than a lower-aspect-ratio wing.

source.document: POF mock exams written by Rihan.pdf
source.notes: The source states both the aspect-ratio definition and the high-AR/low-AR induced-drag relationship.

brief.student_must_understand: High aspect ratio means relatively long span and short mean chord, and it reduces induced drag compared with a low-aspect-ratio wing.
refine: Use top-view high-AR versus low-AR planforms
Make the span/chord ratio visually obvious
Show weaker versus stronger wingtip-vortex/induced-drag cue without adding unsupported numbers
add: HIGH AR: longer span / shorter chord
LOW AR: shorter span / broader chord

concepts.mapping_reason: Four rows test the same aspect-ratio geometry and its induced-drag consequence.

concepts.concept: Anhedral is the wing geometry in which the wings slope downward from root to tip when viewed from the front.

source.location: Question 55; geometry cross-check against PHAK Figure 1-27 dihedral definition
source.notes: The question source explicitly defines downward root-to-tip inclination as anhedral; PHAK Figure 1-27 provides the opposite dihedral geometry for a clean contrast.

brief.student_must_understand: From a front view, anhedral means each wingtip sits lower than its wing root; it is the opposite geometric sense of dihedral.
refine: Use anhedral as the dominant panel with a small dihedral contrast inset only if needed
Keep stability implications secondary to the geometry
Avoid perspective that makes the slope ambiguous

concepts.mapping_reason: Question 2004 directly tests recognition of anhedral geometry.
